name: Sabudana Khichdi
ingredients: 1 cup sabudana (soaked 5-6 hours), 2 medium potatoes (boiled, cubed), ½ cup roasted peanuts (coarsely crushed), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds (jeera), 2 green chillies (finely chopped), 8-10 curry leaves, 1 tsp sendha namak (rock salt), 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander leaves (chopped)
preparation: STEP 1: Wash sabudana 3-4 times in water until water runs clear (removes excess starch). Soak in ¾ cup water for 5-6 hours or overnight — the water should be JUST enough to cover the pearls. STEP 2: After soaking, test one pearl by pressing between fingers — it should mash easily. Drain any excess water. STEP 3: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a non-stick pan on medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter (about 15 seconds). STEP 4: Add green chillies and curry leaves. Sauté for 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add boiled potato cubes. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden. STEP 6: Add the drained sabudana, crushed peanuts, sendha namak, and sugar. Mix gently. STEP 7: Cook on medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring gently, until sabudana turns translucent. Do NOT overcook or it becomes sticky. STEP 8: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve immediately.
tips: CRITICAL TIP: The soaking is the make-or-break step. Too much water = mushy; too little = hard pearls. Test one pearl before cooking. Use non-stick pan to avoid sticking. Serve immediately — it hardens on standing.

name: Kuttu Ki Puri
ingredients: 1 cup kuttu (buckwheat) flour, 2 medium potatoes (boiled, mashed), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 green chilli (chopped fine), water as needed (about 2-3 tbsp), oil for deep frying (about 2 cups)
preparation: STEP 1: In a large bowl, combine kuttu flour and mashed boiled potato. The potato acts as a binder (kuttu flour has no gluten). STEP 2: Add sendha namak, black pepper, and green chilli. STEP 3: Mix with fingertips first, then knead into a soft dough. Add water only 1 tbsp at a time — kuttu absorbs water differently than wheat. Dough should be soft but not sticky. STEP 4: Cover and rest for 10 minutes. STEP 5: Divide into 8-10 small balls. Grease palms with a little oil (kuttu dough is sticky). STEP 6: Flatten each ball between two greased plastic sheets or on a greased surface — kuttu puris break easily on regular rolling. Roll into small 3-4 inch circles. STEP 7: Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium-high heat. Test with a small piece — it should sizzle immediately. STEP 8: Slide one puri gently into hot oil. Press lightly with slotted spoon until it puffs (10-15 seconds). Flip and fry until golden (20-30 seconds more). STEP 9: Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with aloo sabzi or curd.
tips: IMPORTANT: Do not skip the boiled potato — kuttu has no gluten and won't hold shape without a binder. Roll on greased surface, not with dry flour dusting. Fry on medium-high heat quickly, else puris absorb oil.

name: Singhare Ki Kadhi
ingredients: 3 tbsp singhara (water chestnut) flour, 1½ cups curd (whisked), 3 cups water, 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 dry red chillies, 8 curry leaves, ¼ tsp turmeric (optional — some avoid on Ekadashi), 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, whisk curd until smooth. Add singhara flour and whisk to a smooth paste with no lumps. Add 3 cups water gradually while whisking. STEP 2: Transfer to a heavy-bottomed pan. Add sendha namak, black pepper, and optional turmeric. STEP 3: Cook on medium heat, stirring CONTINUOUSLY for the first 5 minutes to prevent curdling. STEP 4: Once it comes to a boil, reduce to low heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Kadhi should thicken slightly. STEP 5: In a small pan, heat ghee. Add cumin seeds — let them splutter. Add dry red chillies and curry leaves. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 6: Pour this tempering over the kadhi. STEP 7: Garnish with coriander. Serve hot with kuttu puri or sama ke chawal.
tips: The CONTINUOUS stirring at the start is essential — otherwise curd curdles into lumps. Singhara flour thickens as it cools, so keep it slightly thin.

name: Sama Ke Chawal Pulao
ingredients: 1 cup sama ke chawal (barnyard millet), 2 cups water, 1 medium potato (cubed), ½ cup peanuts, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 2 green chillies, 8 curry leaves, 1 tsp sendha namak, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Wash sama chawal twice — the water should run mostly clear. Drain. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Add cumin — let it splutter. Add green chillies, curry leaves, peanuts. Sauté 1 minute until peanuts are lightly golden. STEP 3: Add cubed potato. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 4: Add washed sama chawal. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 5: Add 2 cups water and sendha namak. Stir gently. STEP 6: Close pressure cooker. Cook on medium heat for 2 whistles (about 8-10 minutes). Turn off. STEP 7: Let pressure release naturally (5-7 minutes). Open, fluff with fork. STEP 8: Add lemon juice and coriander. Mix gently. Serve hot with curd.
tips: Sama chawal cooks like rice but is a millet — fully allowed on Ekadashi. Use 2:1 water ratio. Do not open cooker while pressure is on.

name: Aloo Ki Sabzi (Vrat Style)
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (boiled, peeled, cubed), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 green chillies (slit), ½ inch ginger (grated — optional for strict Ekadashi), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tomato (chopped — some avoid), 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander leaves, ½ cup water
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds — let them splutter. STEP 2: Add green chillies and grated ginger (if using). Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 3: Add chopped tomato (if using). Cook 3-4 minutes until soft. STEP 4: Add boiled potato cubes. Sauté 2 minutes. Lightly mash some with the back of the spoon for thicker gravy. STEP 5: Add sendha namak, black pepper, and ½ cup water. STEP 6: Simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes, until gravy thickens slightly. STEP 7: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve hot with kuttu puri.
tips: This is the classic Ekadashi/vrat-style aloo sabzi. Ginger and tomato are used in liberal traditions; strict observers skip both. Ask user preference.

name: Rajgira Paratha
ingredients: 1 cup rajgira (amaranth) flour, 1 medium potato (boiled, mashed), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp cumin powder, 1 green chilli (finely chopped), 2 tbsp coriander leaves, ghee for cooking (about 3 tbsp), water as needed
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, combine rajgira flour and mashed potato. STEP 2: Add sendha namak, cumin powder, chopped green chilli, and coriander. STEP 3: Knead into a soft dough using minimal water (1-2 tbsp). Rajgira dough is delicate. STEP 4: Rest for 10 minutes. STEP 5: Divide into 6 balls. Roll each between two greased plastic sheets (rajgira breaks like kuttu). Make small, thick parathas (thinner than kuttu). STEP 6: Heat a tawa on medium heat. Transfer paratha carefully. STEP 7: Cook 30 seconds. Flip. Apply ghee. Cook 1 minute. Flip and apply ghee on the other side. Press gently with spatula for even cooking. STEP 8: Cook until golden brown on both sides (about 3 minutes total). Serve hot with curd or aloo sabzi.
tips: Rajgira is highly nutritious — protein, iron, calcium. Roll thicker than regular parathas. Do not use dry flour for dusting — use greased surface.

name: Makhana Kheer
ingredients: 1 cup makhana (fox nuts), 1 litre full-fat milk, ½ cup sugar (or jaggery), 10 cashews (chopped), 10 almonds (slivered), 10 raisins, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp ghee, few strands of saffron (kesar) soaked in 1 tbsp warm milk
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add makhana. Roast on low-medium heat for 5-7 minutes until crisp. STEP 2: Remove half the makhana and crush coarsely (this thickens the kheer). Keep the other half whole. STEP 3: In the same pan, pour milk. Bring to a boil. STEP 4: Reduce heat. Add both crushed and whole makhana. STEP 5: Simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring often to prevent burning at the bottom. Milk should reduce by about 30%. STEP 6: Add sugar and stir until dissolved (2 minutes). STEP 7: Add chopped cashews, almonds, and raisins. STEP 8: Add cardamom powder and saffron milk. STEP 9: Simmer 2 more minutes. Serve warm or chilled.
tips: Makhana kheer is a classic Ekadashi dessert — no grains, only dairy and fox nuts. Use full-fat milk for richness. Can be made with jaggery for a healthier version.

name: Sabudana Vada
ingredients: 1 cup sabudana (soaked 5-6 hours), 2 medium potatoes (boiled, mashed), ½ cup roasted peanuts (coarsely crushed), 2 green chillies (finely chopped), 1 inch ginger (grated), 2 tbsp coriander leaves, 1 tsp sendha namak, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tbsp lemon juice, oil for deep frying
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked sabudana completely. Place in a large bowl. STEP 2: Add mashed potato, crushed peanuts, green chillies, ginger, coriander, sendha namak, cumin seeds, and lemon juice. STEP 3: Mix thoroughly with hands. Mixture should hold shape when pressed — if too wet, add more mashed potato; if too dry, sprinkle water. STEP 4: Divide into 12-15 lemon-sized balls. Flatten slightly into thick discs. STEP 5: Heat oil in a kadai on medium heat. Test with a small piece — it should rise up gradually with bubbles. STEP 6: Slide 3-4 vadas at a time into hot oil. Do not overcrowd. STEP 7: Fry on medium heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. STEP 8: Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with curd or coconut chutney.
tips: CRITICAL: Oil must be at medium temperature, not too hot. High heat browns outside but leaves inside raw. Do not skip peanuts — they hold the vada together and add crunch.

name: Shakarkandi Chaat
ingredients: 3 medium sweet potatoes (shakarkandi), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander leaves, 1 green chilli (chopped), ¼ cup pomegranate seeds (garnish)
preparation: STEP 1: Boil sweet potatoes with skin in salted water for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender. Cool, peel, and cube. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pan on medium heat. Add cubed sweet potatoes. STEP 3: Sauté for 5-7 minutes until edges caramelize slightly. STEP 4: Turn off heat. Transfer to a bowl. STEP 5: Add sendha namak, black pepper, cumin powder, lemon juice, green chilli, and coriander. Toss gently. STEP 6: Garnish with pomegranate seeds. Serve warm.
tips: Sweet potato is naturally sweet, filling, and fully Ekadashi-safe. Roasted cumin powder adds a distinctive chaat flavour.

name: Vrat Wale Chaawal Ki Kheer
ingredients: ½ cup sama ke chawal (washed), 1 litre full-fat milk, ½ cup sugar, 8 cashews (chopped), 8 almonds (slivered), 1 tbsp raisins, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp ghee
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan. Add drained sama chawal. Roast on low heat for 2 minutes. STEP 2: Add milk. Bring to a boil. STEP 3: Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, stirring often to prevent burning. The sama chawal will cook and thicken the milk. STEP 4: Once chawal is soft and milk has reduced by about 30%, add sugar. Stir until dissolved. STEP 5: Add cashews, almonds, and raisins. Cook 2 minutes. STEP 6: Add cardamom powder. Turn off heat. STEP 7: Serve warm or chilled.
tips: Sama chawal kheer is a great Ekadashi dessert — resembles regular rice kheer but is grain-free.

name: Peanut Ladoo (Vrat)
ingredients: 1 cup roasted peanuts (skinned), ½ cup jaggery (chopped small), 1 tbsp ghee, ¼ tsp cardamom powder
preparation: STEP 1: Grind roasted peanuts coarsely (not to powder — should have texture). STEP 2: In a pan, heat ghee on low heat. Add jaggery. Melt slowly until it forms a thick syrup (about 3-4 minutes). Do NOT let it caramelize dark. STEP 3: Turn off heat. Add crushed peanuts and cardamom powder. Mix quickly. STEP 4: While mixture is still warm (not hot enough to burn hands), grease palms with ghee and roll into small ladoos (about 12). STEP 5: Cool completely before storing. Keeps for 2 weeks.
tips: Quick, filling, and travel-friendly. Great for morning of a fasting day.

name: Fruit and Nut Bowl
ingredients: 1 apple (chopped), 1 banana (sliced), 1 pomegranate (seeded), ½ cup grapes, 5 dates (chopped), 10 almonds (soaked, peeled), 10 cashews, 1 tbsp raisins, 1 tsp chia seeds, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp honey (optional)
preparation: STEP 1: In a large bowl, combine all chopped fruits. STEP 2: Add dates, almonds, cashews, and raisins. STEP 3: Sprinkle chia seeds and cardamom powder. STEP 4: Drizzle honey if using. Toss gently. STEP 5: Serve immediately — do not let sit or fruits will release water.
tips: The simplest Ekadashi meal. Zero cooking needed. Great for busy mornings or as a light dinner.

name: Kuttu Ki Roti
ingredients: 1 cup kuttu (buckwheat) flour, 1 medium boiled potato (mashed), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp ajwain (carom seeds) — optional, ghee for cooking (about 2 tbsp), water as needed (about ¼ cup)
preparation: STEP 1: In a mixing bowl, combine kuttu flour with mashed boiled potato and sendha namak. Add ajwain if using. STEP 2: Add water 1 tbsp at a time and knead into a soft, non-sticky dough. Cover and rest for 10 minutes. STEP 3: Divide into 6 equal balls. Grease your palms and a plastic sheet with a little ghee. STEP 4: Place a ball on the sheet. Cover with another sheet. Roll into a 5-6 inch circle. Kuttu breaks easily — roll thicker than regular roti. STEP 5: Heat tawa on medium heat. Carefully transfer roti. STEP 6: Cook 30 seconds on one side. Flip. Apply ½ tsp ghee. Cook 1 minute. Flip again. Apply ghee on the other side. Press gently. STEP 7: Cook until brown spots appear on both sides (about 3 minutes total). Serve hot with aloo tamatar sabzi or curd.
tips: Add mashed potato is CRITICAL — kuttu has no gluten. Roll on greased surface, not with dry flour. Cook on medium heat, not high.

name: Farali Aloo Tamatar Sabzi
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (boiled, cubed), 3 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 green chillies (slit), 1 inch ginger (grated — optional), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tsp red chilli powder (Kashmiri), ¼ tsp turmeric (optional), 2 tbsp coriander leaves, 1 cup water
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin seeds — let splutter. STEP 2: Add green chillies and ginger. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 3: Add chopped tomatoes. Cook 5-6 minutes until tomatoes are soft and mushy. STEP 4: Add sendha namak, red chilli powder, and optional turmeric. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add cubed boiled potatoes. Mix gently. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 6: Add 1 cup water. Bring to a boil. STEP 7: Simmer on low heat for 5-7 minutes until gravy thickens. STEP 8: Add black pepper and coriander. Serve hot with kuttu roti or puri.
tips: This is the classic Navratri combo with kuttu roti. Some families avoid turmeric; ask user. Tomato-based, so avoid on Friday fast (no-sour rule).

name: Singhare Ka Halwa
ingredients: 1 cup singhara (water chestnut) flour, ½ cup ghee, ¾ cup sugar, 2 cups water, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 10 chopped cashews, 10 chopped almonds, 1 tbsp raisins
preparation: STEP 1: In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat ghee on medium heat. Add singhara flour. STEP 2: Roast on low-medium heat, stirring continuously, for 10-12 minutes until it turns golden brown and releases aroma. This is the most important step — do not rush. STEP 3: In a separate pan, boil 2 cups water. STEP 4: Slowly add hot water to the roasted flour, stirring vigorously to avoid lumps. Be careful — it will splutter. STEP 5: Cook for 3-4 minutes until it thickens. STEP 6: Add sugar and cardamom powder. Stir until sugar dissolves (2 minutes). STEP 7: Add cashews, almonds, and raisins. Cook 1 minute. STEP 8: Serve hot.
tips: The roasting of flour in ghee is the flavour foundation. Under-roasted = raw taste; over-roasted = bitter. Stir constantly on low-medium heat.

name: Samo Rice Pulao
ingredients: 1 cup sama ke chawal (barnyard millet), 2 cups water, 1 medium potato (cubed), ½ cup carrot equivalent — use bottle gourd (lauki) cubed instead if strict, ½ cup green peas, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 2 green chillies, 1 inch ginger (grated), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp garam masala, 2 tbsp coriander leaves, 10 cashews
preparation: STEP 1: Wash sama chawal twice. Drain. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add cashews. Sauté 30 seconds until golden. STEP 4: Add green chillies and ginger. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add potato and lauki cubes and peas. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 6: Add sama chawal, sendha namak, and garam masala. Mix. STEP 7: Add 2 cups water. Stir. STEP 8: Close cooker. 2 whistles on medium heat. STEP 9: Let pressure release naturally. Fluff with fork. Garnish with coriander. Serve with curd.
tips: A wholesome Navratri one-pot meal. Peas are allowed in most Navratri traditions. Sama chawal is filling and nutritious.

name: Kaddu Ki Sabzi
ingredients: 500g pumpkin (kaddu — peeled, seeded, cubed), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 green chillies (slit), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp fennel powder (saunf), 1 tbsp jaggery (grated), 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ghee in a kadai. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 2: Add green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add pumpkin cubes. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 4: Add sendha namak, red chilli powder, and fennel powder. Mix. STEP 5: Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring 2-3 times. Pumpkin releases water and cooks in its own moisture. STEP 6: Once tender, add jaggery. Mix gently, mashing some pumpkin for a semi-mashed texture. STEP 7: Cook 2 more minutes. Turn off heat. STEP 8: Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve with kuttu roti.
tips: Sweet-tangy pumpkin sabzi is a Navratri classic. Jaggery balances the tanginess. Pumpkin is naturally sweet and cooks fast.

name: Sabudana Vada
ingredients: Same as Ekadashi Sabudana Vada (E008) — use same recipe
preparation: Refer to Recipe E008 in Ekadashi Recipes sheet. Same preparation method — Navratri-safe.
tips: This is one of the most popular Navratri snacks across India.

name: Lauki Kofta (Navratri)
ingredients: FOR KOFTAS: 1 medium bottle gourd (lauki — grated, squeezed dry), ½ cup singhara flour, 1 green chilli (chopped), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper. FOR GRAVY: 3 tomatoes (pureed), ½ cup curd (whisked), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 1 green chilli, 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder, 1 tbsp cream (optional), oil for frying koftas
preparation: STEP 1 (KOFTAS): Squeeze grated lauki very well — remove all water (save the water for gravy). STEP 2: In a bowl, combine squeezed lauki, singhara flour, green chilli, sendha namak, and black pepper. Mix to form a soft dough. STEP 3: Shape into small balls (about 10). STEP 4: Heat oil for deep frying on medium heat. Fry koftas until golden brown (about 3-4 minutes). Drain on paper towel. STEP 5 (GRAVY): Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. Add green chilli. STEP 6: Add tomato puree. Cook 5-7 minutes until oil separates. STEP 7: Add sendha namak, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 8: Reduce heat. Slowly add whisked curd, stirring continuously to prevent curdling. STEP 9: Add ½ cup of the reserved lauki water. Simmer 5 minutes. STEP 10: Add cream if using. STEP 11: Gently drop koftas into gravy. Simmer 2 minutes (don't stir vigorously — koftas break). Serve hot with kuttu roti.
tips: Squeezing lauki is critical — excess water = koftas fall apart in oil. Add koftas to gravy just before serving to keep them intact.

name: Vrat Wale Dahi Vada
ingredients: FOR VADA: 1 cup sabudana (soaked), 2 boiled potatoes (mashed), 1 tsp sendha namak, 1 green chilli, oil for frying. FOR SERVING: 2 cups thick curd (whisked, chilled), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, 1 tsp jaggery syrup, coriander for garnish
preparation: STEP 1: Prepare sabudana vadas as in Recipe E008. Fry until golden. STEP 2: Soak vadas in warm water for 5 minutes. Squeeze gently and set aside. STEP 3: In a serving bowl, whisk cold curd with sendha namak, black pepper, and jaggery syrup until smooth. STEP 4: Arrange soaked vadas on plate. Pour whisked curd over them. STEP 5: Sprinkle roasted cumin powder and coriander. Serve immediately.
tips: A cooling Navratri snack, great for the hot days of early Navratri. Chill the curd well.

name: Rajgira Ladoo
ingredients: 1 cup rajgira (puffed amaranth), ½ cup jaggery (chopped), 2 tbsp ghee, ¼ cup chopped mixed nuts (cashew, almond), ¼ tsp cardamom powder
preparation: STEP 1: In a pan, heat ghee on low. Add jaggery. Melt slowly until thick syrup forms (3-4 minutes). Test: drop syrup in cold water — it should form a soft ball. STEP 2: Turn off heat. Immediately add puffed rajgira and chopped nuts. Mix quickly. STEP 3: Add cardamom powder. STEP 4: While warm (not hot), grease palms with ghee. Roll into small ladoos (about 10-12). STEP 5: Cool completely. Store in airtight container. Keeps for 15 days.
tips: Rajgira is very rich in calcium and protein. Perfect Navratri snack.

name: Farali Chivda
ingredients: 1 cup roasted peanuts, 1 cup roasted makhana (fox nuts), ½ cup raisins, ¼ cup chopped cashews, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies (chopped fine), 1 tsp sendha namak, 1 tsp powdered sugar, ½ tsp black pepper
preparation: STEP 1: Roast makhana in dry pan for 5 minutes until crisp. Set aside. STEP 2: In the same pan, heat ghee. Add cumin, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 3: Add roasted peanuts and cashews. Roast 1 minute. STEP 4: Add roasted makhana, raisins. Mix. STEP 5: Turn off heat. Add sendha namak, powdered sugar, and black pepper. Toss well. STEP 6: Cool completely. Store in airtight container. Keeps for 2 weeks.
tips: The perfect Navratri travel snack. Balances sweet, salty, spicy. Sugar is a Maharashtrian farali touch.

name: Vrat Dahi Aloo
ingredients: 4 boiled potatoes (cubed), 1 cup thick curd (whisked), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 green chillies (slit), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: Whisk curd until smooth. Add sendha namak and black pepper. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add green chillies. Sauté 15 seconds. STEP 4: Add boiled potatoes. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 5: Reduce heat to LOW. Slowly add whisked curd, stirring continuously. STEP 6: Cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes. Do not boil — curd will curdle. STEP 7: Sprinkle roasted cumin powder and coriander. Serve with kuttu roti.
tips: Very low heat is critical when curd is added. This is a comforting, mild sabzi.

name: Sabudana Kheer
ingredients: ½ cup sabudana (soaked 2 hours), 1 litre full-fat milk, ½ cup sugar, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 10 chopped almonds, 10 chopped cashews, 1 tbsp raisins, few strands saffron
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked sabudana. STEP 2: In a heavy-bottomed pan, bring milk to a boil. STEP 3: Reduce heat. Add sabudana. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until sabudana turns transparent and milk thickens. STEP 4: Add sugar. Stir until dissolved (2 minutes). STEP 5: Add cardamom powder, saffron, and dry fruits. STEP 6: Cook 2 more minutes. Serve warm or chilled.
tips: A creamy, comforting Navratri dessert. Do not over-soak sabudana — 2 hours is enough for kheer.

name: Arbi Ki Sabzi (Farali)
ingredients: 500g arbi (colocasia — boiled, peeled, cubed), 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 2 green chillies (slit), 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp coriander powder — some skip, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: Boil arbi with skin for 15-20 minutes until fork-tender. Cool, peel, and cube. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add green chillies. Sauté 15 seconds. STEP 4: Add arbi cubes. Sauté on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until edges get crispy. STEP 5: Add sendha namak, red chilli powder, and coriander powder. Toss well. STEP 6: Sauté 2 more minutes. STEP 7: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve with kuttu roti.
tips: Arbi is allowed on Navratri (technically a root vegetable but treated as fasting-safe). Boil separately, then pan-fry for texture.

name: Fruit Chaat (Navratri)
ingredients: 1 apple, 1 banana, 1 pear, 1 pomegranate (seeded), 1 cup grapes, 1 orange (segmented), 10 chopped dates, 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp mint leaves (chopped)
preparation: STEP 1: Wash and chop all fruits into bite-sized pieces. STEP 2: In a large bowl, combine all fruits. STEP 3: Add dates. STEP 4: Sprinkle sendha namak, roasted cumin powder, and black pepper. STEP 5: Add lemon juice and mint. Toss gently. STEP 6: Serve immediately.
tips: The simplest Navratri snack. Chaat masala can be made at home (roasted cumin + dried mango powder — check amchur is farali).

name: Kuttu Ka Chilla
ingredients: 1 cup kuttu flour, 1 boiled potato (grated), 1 green chilli (chopped), 2 tbsp coriander leaves, 1 tsp sendha namak, ½ tsp cumin seeds, ¾ cup water (adjust), ghee for cooking
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, mix kuttu flour, grated potato, green chilli, coriander, sendha namak, and cumin. STEP 2: Slowly add water and whisk to a smooth pouring batter (like dosa batter). Let rest 5 minutes. STEP 3: Heat a non-stick pan on medium heat. Grease with ghee. STEP 4: Pour a ladleful of batter. Spread in a circle. STEP 5: Cook 2 minutes until bottom is golden. Drizzle ½ tsp ghee around edges. Flip. STEP 6: Cook 1 minute on the other side. Serve with curd or fruit chaat.
tips: A quick Navratri breakfast. Add grated bottle gourd for extra volume. Perfect for busy mornings.

name: Jain Pav Bhaji
ingredients: 2 cups raw banana (peeled, cubed) — replaces potato, 1 cup pumpkin/kaddu (cubed), 1 cup lauki/bottle gourd (cubed), ½ cup green peas, ½ cup cauliflower florets, 1 capsicum (diced), 3 tomatoes (chopped), 2 tbsp pav bhaji masala, 1 tsp red chilli powder, ¼ tsp turmeric, 3 tbsp butter, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 3 tbsp coriander, 8 pav (Jain pav — no onion), 2 tbsp butter for pav
preparation: STEP 1: In a pressure cooker, add raw banana, pumpkin, lauki, peas, and cauliflower with 1 cup water and salt. Pressure cook for 3 whistles. STEP 2: Once cool, mash the vegetables coarsely. STEP 3: In a large pan, heat 2 tbsp butter. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 4: Add chopped tomatoes and capsicum. Cook 8-10 minutes until soft and mushy. STEP 5: Add pav bhaji masala, red chilli powder, and turmeric. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 6: Add the mashed vegetables. Mix well. STEP 7: Add 1 cup water. Simmer for 10 minutes, mashing further with the back of the spoon. STEP 8: Adjust salt. Add 1 tbsp butter and lemon juice. STEP 9: For pav: Slit pav horizontally. Toast on tawa with butter until crisp. STEP 10: Serve bhaji hot, topped with butter, coriander, and pav on the side.
tips: The KEY substitution: raw banana replaces potato beautifully. Lauki adds bulk. Some Jain families accept capsicum, others avoid. Ensure pav is Jain-friendly (many bakeries make special Jain pav without onion).

name: Jain Palak Paneer
ingredients: 2 bunches spinach (palak — washed, blanched), 250g paneer (cubed), 2 tomatoes (pureed), 1 green chilli, 1 inch cinnamon, 2 cloves, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp garam masala, ½ cup fresh cream, 1 tsp jeera powder
preparation: STEP 1: Blanch spinach: boil water, add spinach, cook 2 minutes, drain, plunge in ice water. Squeeze dry. STEP 2: Blend blanched spinach with green chilli to a smooth puree. STEP 3: Lightly pan-fry paneer cubes in 1 tsp ghee until golden edges. Set aside. STEP 4: Heat remaining ghee in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 5: Add cinnamon and cloves. Sauté 15 seconds. STEP 6: Add tomato puree. Cook 5-7 minutes until oil separates. STEP 7: Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 8: Add spinach puree. Mix well. Cook on low heat 5 minutes. STEP 9: Add ½ cup water for consistency. STEP 10: Add paneer cubes and cream. Simmer 3 minutes. STEP 11: Sprinkle garam masala and jeera powder. Serve with roti or naan.
tips: NO onion, NO garlic, NO ginger — pure Jain. Tomato-cream base gives richness without alliums. Some strict Jain families avoid palak (green leafy) during Paryushana.

name: Kele Ki Sabzi (Raw Banana)
ingredients: 3 raw bananas (peeled, cubed), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies (slit), ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp jaggery (grated), 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Peel raw bananas (they are sticky — grease hands with oil first). Cut into ½ inch cubes. Immediately soak in salted water to prevent browning. STEP 2: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 3: Add curry leaves and green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add drained raw banana cubes. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 5: Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Mix. STEP 6: Add ¼ cup water. Cover and cook on low heat for 10-12 minutes until bananas are tender. STEP 7: Add jaggery. Mix gently. Cook 2 minutes. STEP 8: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve hot.
tips: The classic Jain substitute for aloo sabzi. Raw banana has similar texture to potato when cooked. Soak in salt water to prevent oxidation.

name: Tendli Ki Sabzi
ingredients: 500g tendli (ivy gourd — sliced lengthwise), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp asafoetida (hing), ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp roasted peanut powder (optional), 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Wash tendli. Slice lengthwise into 4 pieces each (removing hard ends). STEP 2: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 3: Add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add sliced tendli. Sauté 3-4 minutes. STEP 5: Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Mix. STEP 6: Cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tendli is tender. STEP 7: Add jaggery and peanut powder. Mix. Cook 2 minutes. STEP 8: Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve with roti or thepla.
tips: Tendli is one of the most Jain-friendly vegetables. Peanut powder adds richness (skip during Paryushana Ayambil).

name: Jain Dal (Osaman)
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal (arhar), 4 cups water, 2 tomatoes (chopped — some skip), 2 tbsp jaggery (grated), 1 tbsp lemon juice or 3 kokum petals, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp mustard seeds, ¼ tsp asafoetida (hing), 8 curry leaves, 2 dry red chillies, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Wash toor dal. Pressure cook with 4 cups water and turmeric for 4 whistles. Once cooked, whisk to a smooth consistency. STEP 2: Transfer dal to a pot. Add chopped tomatoes, jaggery, and salt. Bring to a boil. STEP 3: Simmer 10 minutes until tomatoes are soft. STEP 4: In a small pan, heat ghee. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin, asafoetida, curry leaves, and dry red chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 5: Pour tempering over dal. STEP 6: Add lemon juice or kokum. STEP 7: Simmer 2 more minutes. Garnish with coriander. Serve with steamed rice.
tips: The classic Gujarati Jain dal — sweet, sour, and savoury. Kokum is more traditional than lemon. Hing replaces the missing onion-garlic flavour.

name: Jain Cabbage Sabzi
ingredients: ½ medium cabbage (shredded), 1 capsicum (diced), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp sugar, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 2: Add asafoetida, curry leaves, and green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add shredded cabbage and diced capsicum. Toss well. STEP 4: Add turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and sugar. Mix. STEP 5: Cook on medium-high heat, uncovered, for 5-7 minutes, stirring often. Cabbage should retain some crunch. STEP 6: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve with roti or dal-chawal.
tips: Cook cabbage uncovered on higher heat to retain crunch and prevent mushy texture.

name: Methi Thepla (Jain)
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat flour, ½ cup besan (chickpea flour), 1 cup fresh methi (fenugreek — chopped fine), 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp jaggery, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp sesame seeds, ¼ cup curd, ¼ cup oil (for dough), oil for cooking
preparation: STEP 1: In a large bowl, mix wheat flour, besan, chopped methi, turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, jaggery, asafoetida, and sesame seeds. STEP 2: Add curd and oil. Mix. STEP 3: Gradually add water and knead into a soft but firm dough. Rest 15 minutes. STEP 4: Divide into 10-12 balls. Roll each into a thin round (thepla should be thinner than paratha). STEP 5: Heat tawa on medium heat. Place thepla on tawa. STEP 6: When bubbles appear (30 seconds), flip. Apply ½ tsp oil. Cook 1 minute. Flip again, apply oil, and press with spatula for even cooking. STEP 7: Cook until brown spots appear on both sides. STEP 8: Serve with curd, jaggery, or pickle.
tips: Some Jain families avoid methi during Paryushana (green leafy). Thepla stays fresh for 2-3 days — great travel food.

name: Dudhi Chana Dal Sabzi
ingredients: 1 medium bottle gourd (dudhi/lauki — peeled, cubed), ½ cup chana dal (soaked 2 hours), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 cup water, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked chana dal. STEP 2: Heat oil in a pressure cooker. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 3: Add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add soaked chana dal. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 5: Add cubed dudhi. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 6: Add turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and 1 cup water. Mix. STEP 7: Close pressure cooker. 3 whistles on medium heat. STEP 8: Once pressure releases, open cooker. Add jaggery and lemon juice. Mix. STEP 9: If watery, cook uncovered 2-3 minutes to thicken. Garnish with coriander. Serve with roti.
tips: A wholesome combination of dal + vegetable. Dudhi is very Jain-friendly (grown above ground). Balanced macros — protein + fibre.

name: Sev Tameta Nu Shaak
ingredients: 4 large tomatoes (chopped), 1 cup thick sev (Jain — no onion/garlic), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, 1 cup water, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 2: Add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add chopped tomatoes. Cook 5-7 minutes until soft and mushy. STEP 4: Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 5: Add 1 cup water and jaggery. Bring to a boil. STEP 6: Simmer 3-4 minutes. STEP 7: Turn off heat. IMMEDIATELY before serving, add sev and mix gently. STEP 8: Garnish with coriander. Serve hot with roti or thepla. Sev softens quickly — serve immediately.
tips: Add sev at the very last moment or it becomes soggy. This is a Gujarati Jain staple — quick, filling, and flavourful without alliums.

name: Jain Paneer Sabzi
ingredients: 250g paneer (cubed), 3 tomatoes (pureed), ¼ cup cashew paste (10 cashews soaked, blended), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp garam masala, 2 tbsp fresh cream, 2 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek)
preparation: STEP 1: Lightly sauté paneer cubes in 1 tsp ghee until edges are golden. Set aside. STEP 2: Heat remaining ghee. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add asafoetida and green chillies. Sauté 15 seconds. STEP 4: Add tomato puree. Cook 7-8 minutes until oil separates. STEP 5: Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 6: Add cashew paste. Mix well. Cook 3 minutes. STEP 7: Add ¾ cup water. Simmer 5 minutes. STEP 8: Add paneer cubes. Simmer 3 more minutes. STEP 9: Add cream, garam masala, kasuri methi (crushed between palms), and coriander. STEP 10: Serve hot with roti or naan.
tips: Cashew paste replicates the richness usually provided by onion. Hing is the flavour bridge. Rich, restaurant-style Jain curry.

name: Bajra Khichdi (Paryushana)
ingredients: 1 cup bajra (pearl millet — coarsely broken), ½ cup moong dal, 4 cups water, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp asafoetida, ½ tsp black pepper, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Dry roast bajra in a pan for 5 minutes until aromatic. Cool and coarsely crush in a blender. STEP 2: Wash moong dal. STEP 3: In a pressure cooker, add roasted bajra, moong dal, water, and salt. STEP 4: Pressure cook for 5 whistles. Let pressure release naturally. STEP 5: Open. Mash lightly with the back of a spoon for creamy consistency. STEP 6: In a small pan, heat ghee. Add cumin — let splutter. Add asafoetida. Pour over khichdi. STEP 7: Add black pepper and coriander. Serve hot with ghee, jaggery, and buttermilk.
tips: A traditional Paryushana meal in Gujarati Jain households. Bajra is warming and nutritious. Serve with kaadhi for a complete meal.

name: Ayambil Rice (Plain Boiled)
ingredients: 1 cup rice (any variety), 3 cups water
preparation: STEP 1: Wash rice thoroughly. STEP 2: In a heavy-bottomed pot, add rice and water. STEP 3: Bring to a boil on high heat. STEP 4: Reduce to low heat. Cover partially. Cook for 15-20 minutes until rice is very soft and water is absorbed. STEP 5: Serve as-is. NO oil, NO ghee, NO salt, NO spices, NO sugar. Water only to drink alongside.
tips: This is Ayambil — the strictest Jain fasting food. Deliberately bland. The point is austerity, not taste. Do not add ANYTHING to this dish. One meal per day only, before sunset.

name: Ayambil Moong Dal
ingredients: 1 cup split moong dal, 4 cups water
preparation: STEP 1: Wash moong dal. STEP 2: Pressure cook with 4 cups water for 3 whistles (no salt, no turmeric, no oil, nothing). STEP 3: Open cooker. Serve as-is. Very watery consistency — soup-like. STEP 4: NO tempering, NO salt, NO ghee. Only boiled water alongside.
tips: Second option for Ayambil day. Rotate between different plain boiled grains/pulses each day of the 9-day Navpad Oli to add micro-variety.

name: Jain Puran Poli
ingredients: FOR STUFFING: 1 cup chana dal, 1 cup jaggery (grated), ½ tsp cardamom powder, ¼ tsp nutmeg. FOR DOUGH: 2 cups wheat flour, ¼ cup oil, ½ tsp turmeric, ½ tsp salt, water as needed. FOR SERVING: ghee, milk
preparation: STEP 1 (STUFFING): Pressure cook chana dal with 3 cups water for 4 whistles. Drain excess water (save for kadhi). STEP 2: In a pan, add cooked dal and jaggery. Cook on low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and leaves the sides of the pan (10-12 minutes). STEP 3: Add cardamom and nutmeg. Cool completely. Grind to a smooth paste in a food processor. STEP 4 (DOUGH): Mix flour, oil, turmeric, salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft, elastic dough. Rest 30 minutes covered. STEP 5 (ASSEMBLY): Divide dough into 10 balls and stuffing into 10 slightly larger balls. STEP 6: Flatten a dough ball. Place a stuffing ball in the center. Bring dough edges together and seal. STEP 7: Roll gently into a thin round (like a paratha) — use minimal flour dusting. STEP 8: Heat tawa on medium heat. Cook poli 1 minute on one side. Flip. Apply ghee. Cook another minute. Flip and apply ghee on the other side. STEP 9: Serve hot with ghee and warm milk.
tips: Traditional Diwali/festival sweet. NO onion, NO garlic — naturally Jain-friendly. Time-consuming but worth it for special occasions.

name: Jain Green Moong Sprouts Sabzi
ingredients: 2 cups sprouted green moong, 2 tomatoes (chopped), 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 8 curry leaves, 2 green chillies, ¼ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil in a kadai. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add cumin. STEP 2: Add asafoetida, curry leaves, green chillies. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 3: Add chopped tomatoes. Cook 4-5 minutes until soft. STEP 4: Add turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 5: Add sprouted moong. Mix well. Add ½ cup water. STEP 6: Cover and cook on low heat 8-10 minutes until moong is tender but not mushy. STEP 7: Add jaggery. Mix. Cook 1 minute. STEP 8: Turn off heat. Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve with roti.
tips: IMPORTANT: Some strict Jains avoid sprouts during Paryushana (considered fermented). For non-Paryushana days, sprouts are excellent Jain protein.

name: Sabudana Khichdi (Monday)
ingredients: Refer to Recipe E001 in Ekadashi Recipes
preparation: Refer to Recipe E001. Same recipe — suitable for Monday Shiva fast.
tips: Classic Monday fast meal for Shiva devotees. Ekadashi-format also works for weekly fasts.

name: Sitaphal (Fruit Bowl) — Any Weekly Fast
ingredients: 1 pomegranate (seeded), 1 apple, 1 banana, 1 pear, 10 dates, 10 soaked almonds, 1 tsp honey (optional), ½ tsp cardamom powder
preparation: STEP 1: Chop all fruits. STEP 2: In a large bowl, combine fruits, dates, and almonds. STEP 3: Sprinkle cardamom powder. STEP 4: Drizzle honey if using. Toss gently. Serve immediately.
tips: Universal weekly fast snack. No cooking needed. Works for Monday, Tuesday, Friday, Saturday fasts. Skip honey for Jain family members.

name: Besan Chilla (Tuesday — Red foods)
ingredients: 1 cup besan (chickpea flour), 1 cup water, 1 tomato (finely chopped — red), 1 green chilli, 1 tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp ajwain, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 2 tbsp coriander, oil for cooking
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, whisk besan with water to a smooth pouring batter. Rest 10 minutes. STEP 2: Add chopped tomato, green chilli, red chilli powder, turmeric, salt, ajwain, asafoetida, and coriander. Mix well. STEP 3: Heat a non-stick tawa on medium. Grease with oil. STEP 4: Pour a ladleful of batter. Spread in a circle. STEP 5: Cook 2 minutes. Drizzle ½ tsp oil around edges. Flip. STEP 6: Cook 1 minute. Serve hot with green chutney.
tips: Red foods (tomato, red chilli) fit the Tuesday Hanuman theme. Filling one-meal fast option.

name: Chana Dal Halwa (Thursday — Yellow)
ingredients: 1 cup chana dal (soaked overnight), ¾ cup sugar, ½ cup ghee, 3 cups milk, ½ tsp cardamom powder, few saffron strands, 10 chopped cashews, 10 chopped almonds, 1 tbsp raisins
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked chana dal. Grind to a coarse paste with 2 tbsp water. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a heavy pan. Add ground chana dal. STEP 3: Roast on LOW heat, stirring constantly, for 20-25 minutes. Dal will change colour to golden brown and release aroma. This step is essential — do not rush. STEP 4: In a separate pan, warm milk with sugar until sugar dissolves. STEP 5: Slowly add milk to roasted dal, stirring vigorously to avoid lumps. STEP 6: Cook 5-7 minutes on low heat until it thickens and ghee starts separating. STEP 7: Add cardamom, saffron, cashews, almonds, raisins. Mix. STEP 8: Serve hot.
tips: Yellow dal + turmeric-golden colour = perfect for Thursday (Brihaspati) fast. Rich and filling — this IS the one meal.

name: Banana Sheera (Thursday — Yellow)
ingredients: 1 cup semolina (sooji), 3 ripe bananas (mashed), ½ cup ghee, ¾ cup sugar, 2 cups water, ½ tsp cardamom powder, few saffron strands, 10 chopped cashews, 10 chopped almonds, 1 tbsp raisins
preparation: STEP 1: In a heavy pan, heat ghee. Add sooji. Roast on medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until golden. STEP 2: In a separate pan, boil water with sugar until sugar dissolves. STEP 3: Slowly add hot sugar water to roasted sooji, stirring vigorously. STEP 4: Cook 3-4 minutes until sooji absorbs all water. STEP 5: Add mashed bananas. Mix well. Cook 3 minutes. STEP 6: Add cardamom, saffron, nuts. Serve hot.
tips: Banana + yellow sooji + saffron = triple yellow for Thursday. Also traditional Satyanarayan puja prasad.

name: Coconut Rice (Friday — No Sour)
ingredients: 1 cup basmati rice (cooked, cooled), 1 cup grated coconut, 2 tbsp coconut oil or ghee, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp urad dal, 1 tsp chana dal, 10 curry leaves, 2 dry red chillies, 10 cashews, 1 tsp salt, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil in a large pan. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. STEP 2: Add urad dal and chana dal. Roast until golden (30 seconds). STEP 3: Add cashews. Roast until golden. STEP 4: Add curry leaves, dry red chillies, and asafoetida. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 5: Add grated coconut. Sauté 2-3 minutes on low heat until lightly toasted (do not brown). STEP 6: Add cooked cooled rice and salt. Mix gently. STEP 7: Cook 2 minutes to warm through. Garnish with coriander.
tips: NO tomato, NO lemon, NO tamarind — perfect for Friday fast. Coconut is sacred to Lakshmi.

name: Kheer (Friday — Sweet, No Sour)
ingredients: ½ cup basmati rice (soaked 30 minutes), 1 litre full-fat milk, ½ cup sugar, ½ tsp cardamom powder, few saffron strands, 10 chopped almonds, 10 chopped cashews, 1 tbsp raisins
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked rice. STEP 2: In a heavy-bottomed pan, bring milk to a boil. STEP 3: Add rice. Reduce heat to low. Simmer, stirring often, for 25-30 minutes until rice is soft and milk has reduced by 30%. STEP 4: Add sugar. Stir until dissolved. STEP 5: Add cardamom, saffron, nuts. Cook 3 more minutes. STEP 6: Serve warm or chilled.
tips: The quintessential Friday sweet — no sour, all creamy sweetness. Universal appeal.

name: Urad Dal Vada (Saturday — Black)
ingredients: 1 cup urad dal (soaked 4 hours), 2 green chillies, 1 inch ginger, 10 curry leaves (chopped), ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp black pepper (coarse), 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander, oil for deep frying
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked urad dal. Grind to a thick, fluffy batter using minimal water (2-3 tbsp). Batter should hold shape. STEP 2: Add chopped green chillies, ginger, curry leaves, asafoetida, black pepper, salt, and coriander. Mix well. STEP 3: Heat oil in a deep kadai on medium heat. STEP 4: Wet hands. Take a small ball of batter. Flatten between palms. Make a small hole in the center (donut shape). STEP 5: Slide gently into hot oil. Fry 3-4 vadas at a time. STEP 6: Fry on medium heat 3-4 minutes per side until golden and crisp. STEP 7: Drain on paper towel. Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.
tips: Black urad dal fits the Saturday Shani theme. Traditional South Indian breakfast.

name: Til Ladoo (Saturday — Black)
ingredients: 1 cup black sesame seeds (til), ¾ cup jaggery (grated), 1 tbsp ghee, ¼ tsp cardamom powder
preparation: STEP 1: Dry roast sesame seeds in a pan on low heat for 5 minutes until aromatic. Cool. Coarsely crush half, keep half whole. STEP 2: In a pan, heat ghee. Add jaggery. Melt slowly until thick syrup (3-4 minutes). Test: drop syrup in cold water — should form soft ball. STEP 3: Turn off heat. Immediately add sesame seeds and cardamom. Mix quickly. STEP 4: While warm, grease palms with ghee. Roll into small ladoos (10-12). STEP 5: Cool completely. Store in airtight container. Keeps for 3 weeks.
tips: Black sesame for Saturday. Also traditional for Makar Sankranti. Very rich in calcium and iron.

name: Peanut Chikki (Saturday)
ingredients: 1 cup roasted peanuts (skinned), ¾ cup jaggery, 2 tbsp water, 1 tsp ghee
preparation: STEP 1: Grease a plate or tray with ghee. Keep peanuts nearby. STEP 2: In a pan, heat jaggery with 2 tbsp water on low heat. Melt slowly until thick syrup. Test: drop in cold water — should form a HARD ball (crack stage). STEP 3: Turn off heat. Add roasted peanuts. Mix quickly. STEP 4: Immediately pour onto greased tray. Spread thin with a greased spatula. STEP 5: While still warm, cut into squares or diamonds with a sharp greased knife. STEP 6: Cool completely. Break at cut lines. Store in airtight container. Keeps for a month.
tips: Perfect winter energy snack. Traditional Makar Sankranti sweet too.

name: Dates & Milk Suhoor
ingredients: 6-8 dates (pitted), 2 cups full-fat milk, 4 chopped almonds, 4 chopped cashews, ¼ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp honey (optional)
preparation: STEP 1: Warm milk in a pan on low heat (do not boil). STEP 2: Add cardamom powder. Stir. STEP 3: Pour warm milk into two glasses. STEP 4: Add 3-4 dates per glass. STEP 5: Top with chopped nuts and honey. STEP 6: Serve warm.
tips: The Prophet's Sunnah suhoor. Dates provide slow-releasing energy for the day. Milk keeps you hydrated. Perfect for a light suhoor.

vegan.note: No (skip honey → vegan without milk substitute)

name: Egg-Paratha Suhoor
ingredients: 2 whole wheat parathas (prepared or store-bought), 3 eggs, ¼ cup milk, 1 small tomato (chopped), 2 green chillies (chopped), 1 tbsp coriander, salt to taste, ½ tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp butter or ghee
preparation: STEP 1: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, and black pepper. Add tomato, green chillies, and coriander. STEP 2: Heat butter in a non-stick pan on medium heat. STEP 3: Pour egg mixture. Cook, stirring gently, for 3-4 minutes to soft scrambled eggs. STEP 4: Warm parathas on a tawa. STEP 5: Serve scrambled eggs with warm parathas and a glass of water.
tips: Protein + complex carbs = sustained energy for the fasting day. Add a banana on the side.

name: Oats Porridge with Dry Fruits
ingredients: 1 cup rolled oats, 2 cups milk (or water for vegan), 2 tbsp honey or jaggery, 1 banana (sliced), 10 chopped almonds, 5 dates (chopped), ¼ tsp cardamom powder, ¼ tsp cinnamon powder
preparation: STEP 1: In a saucepan, combine oats and milk. STEP 2: Cook on medium heat, stirring often, for 5-7 minutes until oats are soft. STEP 3: Add honey/jaggery, cardamom, cinnamon. Stir. STEP 4: Turn off heat. Top with banana slices, chopped almonds, and dates. STEP 5: Serve immediately.
tips: Slow-releasing complex carbs keep you full longer. Recommended by dietitians for suhoor.

name: Dates & Water Iftar Opener
ingredients: 4 dates (pitted), 2 glasses water at room temperature
preparation: STEP 1: At the exact time of maghrib (sunset), drink water first. STEP 2: Eat 2-3 dates slowly. STEP 3: Wait 10 minutes before starting the main iftar meal.
tips: The traditional Sunnah way of breaking fast — do not skip. Dates raise blood sugar gently; rushing to heavy food causes indigestion.

name: Fruit Chaat Iftar
ingredients: 1 apple, 1 banana, 1 pear, 1 pomegranate (seeded), 1 cup grapes, 1 orange (segmented), ½ cup melon cubes, 1 tsp chaat masala, ½ tsp black salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp mint leaves (chopped)
preparation: STEP 1: Wash and chop all fruits into bite-sized pieces. STEP 2: In a large bowl, combine all fruits. STEP 3: Add chaat masala, black salt, black pepper, and lemon juice. STEP 4: Add mint. Toss gently. STEP 5: Serve immediately after the dates+water opener.
tips: Rehydrates and provides vitamins after a day of fasting. Do not prepare too early — fruits release water.

name: Rooh Afza Sharbat
ingredients: ¼ cup Rooh Afza syrup, 4 cups cold milk (or water), 1 cup crushed ice, ½ tsp cardamom powder, 2 tbsp chopped almonds (for garnish)
preparation: STEP 1: In a large pitcher, combine Rooh Afza and milk. Whisk well. STEP 2: Add cardamom. STEP 3: Pour into glasses. STEP 4: Add crushed ice and chopped almonds. Serve immediately.
tips: The iconic Ramadan drink. Cooling, sweet, and rehydrating.

name: Hyderabadi Chicken Haleem
ingredients: 500g chicken (boneless, cubed), 1 cup broken wheat (dalia — soaked 1 hour), ¼ cup chana dal, ¼ cup masoor dal, ¼ cup moong dal, ¼ cup urad dal, 2 large onions (sliced, fried), ½ cup ghee, 2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 4 green chillies (chopped), 1 cup curd (whisked), 2 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp haleem masala, 2 tsp salt, 6 cups water, 1 lemon, 1 tbsp mint, 2 tbsp coriander, additional fried onions and ghee for garnish
preparation: STEP 1: Wash and soak wheat and all dals separately for 1 hour. STEP 2: In a large pressure cooker, heat ¼ cup ghee. Add ½ the fried onions. STEP 3: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 4: Add chicken. Sauté 5 minutes until it changes colour. STEP 5: Add curd, red chilli powder, turmeric, haleem masala, and salt. Cook 3 minutes. STEP 6: Add drained wheat and dals. Mix well. STEP 7: Add 6 cups water. Close cooker. STEP 8: Pressure cook 30 minutes on low heat (about 15-20 whistles). STEP 9: Open cooker. Using a wooden mallet or immersion blender, pound/blend the mixture until it becomes a smooth, thick, porridge-like consistency (30 minutes traditional / 5 minutes with blender). STEP 10: Cook uncovered on low heat 15 more minutes, stirring often. Add ½ cup ghee. STEP 11: Serve hot topped with fried onions, mint, coriander, lemon wedges, and drizzled ghee.
tips: The pride of Hyderabadi iftar. Slow-cooked for hours traditionally. Modern shortcut: use pressure cooker + blender. Rich, protein-packed, deeply satisfying.

name: Chicken Biryani (Iftar Feast)
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice (soaked 30 minutes), 750g chicken (bone-in), 2 large onions (sliced, fried), 1 cup curd (whisked), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 3 tbsp biryani masala, 2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 4 green chillies, 2 tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 2 tsp salt, ½ cup ghee, ¼ cup mint (chopped), ¼ cup coriander (chopped), few saffron strands in ¼ cup warm milk, 4 cups water, whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon)
preparation: STEP 1 (MARINATION): Mix chicken with curd, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, ½ the biryani masala, and salt. Marinate 30 minutes. STEP 2 (RICE): Boil 4 cups water with whole spices and 1 tsp salt. Add drained rice. Cook until 70% done (grains should be firm inside). Drain. STEP 3 (CHICKEN): Heat ¼ cup ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add ½ the fried onions and green chillies. STEP 4: Add marinated chicken. Cook covered on medium heat 15 minutes until chicken is cooked and gravy thickens. STEP 5: Add chopped tomatoes and remaining biryani masala. Cook 5 minutes. STEP 6 (LAYERING): Spread half the cooked rice over the chicken. Sprinkle mint, coriander, fried onions. Drizzle 2 tbsp ghee. STEP 7: Add remaining rice on top. Sprinkle remaining mint, coriander, fried onions. Drizzle saffron milk and remaining ghee. STEP 8 (DUM): Cover pot with tight-fitting lid (seal with dough if possible). Cook on very low heat for 20 minutes. STEP 9: Turn off heat. Rest 10 minutes. Do NOT open before resting. STEP 10: Gently fluff. Serve with raita and salan.
tips: The showpiece of iftar/Eid meals. Dum cooking is essential for the layered flavour.

name: Seekh Kebab
ingredients: 500g mutton mince (keema), 1 large onion (grated, squeezed dry), 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 green chillies (chopped), 2 tbsp mint (chopped), 2 tbsp coriander, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp roasted besan, 1 egg, oil for basting, wooden skewers (soaked in water)
preparation: STEP 1: In a large bowl, combine minced meat with all ingredients except besan and egg. Mix thoroughly. STEP 2: Add roasted besan and egg. Mix again — this binds the kebabs. STEP 3: Cover and refrigerate 30 minutes (helps kebabs hold shape). STEP 4: Take a lemon-sized portion. With wet hands, mould around a soaked skewer into a long sausage shape. Press firmly. STEP 5: Repeat for all kebabs (about 8-10). STEP 6: Heat a grill pan or tawa on medium-high heat. Brush with oil. STEP 7: Place kebabs. Cook 3-4 minutes per side, basting with oil, until browned all around and cooked through. STEP 8: Serve hot with mint chutney, sliced onions, and lemon wedges.
tips: Iftar/Eid staple. The grated squeezed onion is critical for keeping kebabs juicy without falling apart.

name: Sheer Khurma
ingredients: 1 cup fine vermicelli (seviyan), 1 litre full-fat milk, ½ cup sugar, 10 dates (chopped), 15 chopped almonds, 15 chopped cashews, 10 chopped pistachios, 2 tbsp raisins, ½ tsp cardamom powder, few saffron strands, 4 tbsp ghee, few rose petals (optional garnish)
preparation: STEP 1: In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat 2 tbsp ghee. Add vermicelli. Roast on low heat for 3-4 minutes until golden brown. Set aside. STEP 2: In another pan, heat remaining ghee. Add cashews and almonds. Roast until golden (30 seconds). Add raisins — puff up briefly. Set aside. STEP 3: In a large heavy-bottomed pan, bring milk to a boil. STEP 4: Add roasted vermicelli and chopped dates. Reduce heat to low. STEP 5: Simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until vermicelli is soft and milk has thickened slightly. STEP 6: Add sugar. Stir until dissolved. STEP 7: Add cardamom powder and saffron. Cook 2 minutes. STEP 8: Turn off heat. Garnish with roasted nuts and rose petals. Serve warm or chilled.
tips: The iconic Eid dessert. Traditionally served for Eid ul-Fitr morning. Also great throughout Ramadan iftar.

name: Vegetable Samosa
ingredients: FOR DOUGH: 2 cups maida (all-purpose flour), 4 tbsp oil, ½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp ajwain, ½ cup water. FOR FILLING: 4 boiled potatoes (mashed coarsely), ½ cup green peas, 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp ginger-green chilli paste, 1 tsp coriander powder, ½ tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp amchur, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander, oil for deep frying
preparation: STEP 1 (DOUGH): Mix flour, oil, salt, ajwain. Rub with fingers until crumbly. Add water gradually to form a stiff dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes. STEP 2 (FILLING): Heat oil. Add cumin — let splutter. Add ginger-chilli paste. Sauté 30 seconds. Add peas. Cook 3 minutes. STEP 3: Add mashed potatoes and all spices. Mix well. Cook 3-4 minutes. Turn off heat. Add coriander. Cool. STEP 4 (ASSEMBLY): Divide dough into 6 balls. Roll each into an oval. Cut in half (creating 12 semicircles). STEP 5: Form each semicircle into a cone. Fill with 2 tbsp filling. Seal the top with water-brushed edges. STEP 6: Heat oil on LOW heat. Fry samosas gently for 8-10 minutes until light golden. STEP 7: Increase heat to medium. Fry 3-4 more minutes until crisp and golden brown. STEP 8: Drain. Serve hot with mint chutney and tamarind chutney.
tips: CRITICAL: LOW HEAT frying is what makes samosas crisp. High heat = brown outside, raw inside. This method is why restaurant samosas are perfect.

name: Falooda
ingredients: 2 tbsp basil seeds (sabja/tukmaria — soaked 15 min), ½ cup falooda sev (cooked), ½ cup Rooh Afza syrup, 3 cups cold milk, 4 scoops vanilla ice cream, 2 tbsp chopped pistachios, 2 tbsp chopped almonds, few rose petals
preparation: STEP 1: Soak basil seeds in 1 cup water for 15 minutes until swollen and translucent. STEP 2: Cook falooda sev per package instructions (usually boil 5 minutes, drain, rinse under cold water). STEP 3: In tall glasses, layer: 1 tbsp Rooh Afza, 1 tbsp soaked basil seeds, 2 tbsp cooked falooda sev. STEP 4: Pour cold milk to fill 3/4 of the glass. STEP 5: Top with a scoop of ice cream. STEP 6: Garnish with pistachios, almonds, and rose petals. Serve immediately with a long spoon.
tips: The most theatrical iftar dessert. All components can be prepared in advance and assembled at iftar time.

name: Karwa Chauth Sargi Thali
ingredients: 2 mathri (savoury crackers), 1 cup sweet vermicelli (seviyan), 1 cup mixed dry fruits (almond, cashew, raisin, pistachio, dates), 1 cup fresh fruits (apple, banana, pomegranate), 1 paratha (aloo or plain), 1 glass milk, 1 cup halwa (any variety), 1 coconut, 4 mithai pieces (barfi, laddoo)
preparation: STEP 1: Prepare seviyan: heat 2 tbsp ghee, roast 1 cup fine vermicelli until golden. Add 2 cups milk and ½ cup sugar. Simmer 10 min. Add cardamom, dry fruits. STEP 2: Prepare halwa (sooji or besan halwa). STEP 3: Warm mathri. STEP 4: Chop fresh fruits. STEP 5: Arrange all items on a thali. STEP 6: Serve to fasting woman BEFORE SUNRISE (typically 4-5 AM). She must eat everything before sunrise as the nirjala fast (no food/water) begins.
tips: The Sargi is traditionally sent by the mother-in-law. Must be nutritious enough to last until moon-sighting at night. Heavy on complex carbs, protein, and slow-release energy.

name: Karwa Chauth Post-Moonrise Dinner
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice (cooked), 1 recipe kadhi (curd-besan curry), 1 recipe rajma or chole, 8 rotis, 1 vegetable sabzi (aloo gobi or paneer), 1 salad, 1 sweet dish (kheer or halwa), 1 kg mithai (assorted)
preparation: STEP 1: Prepare all dishes in the day. STEP 2: After moon sighting (moon sighting happens around 8-9 PM depending on location), the husband gives his wife a sip of water first through a sieve while she looks at his reflection. STEP 3: She then eats a bite of the sweet from his hands. STEP 4: The entire family sits together for the elaborate dinner.
tips: This is a celebration dinner, not fasting food. Traditional Punjabi feast. Sweet is symbolic — starts with sweet.

name: Chhath Thekua
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat flour, 1 cup jaggery, 1 cup water, ½ cup ghee, ¼ cup grated coconut, ¼ tsp cardamom powder, 2 tbsp fennel seeds (saunf), pinch of salt, ghee for deep frying
preparation: STEP 1: Melt jaggery in 1 cup water on low heat. Strain to remove impurities. Cool completely. STEP 2: In a bowl, mix flour, coconut, cardamom, fennel, salt. STEP 3: Add ½ cup ghee. Rub with fingers until crumbly (bread-crumb texture). STEP 4: Add cooled jaggery water slowly, kneading into a stiff dough (like puri dough, NOT soft). STEP 5: Rest 15 minutes. STEP 6: Divide into small balls. Flatten each. Press onto a thekua mould (or make patterns with a fork). STEP 7: Heat ghee for deep frying on LOW heat. STEP 8: Fry thekua on low heat for 5-6 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Do NOT increase heat — thekuas will brown outside but stay raw inside. STEP 9: Drain. Cool completely on wire rack. Store in airtight container. Keeps 15 days.
tips: The sacred Chhath prasad. STRICTLY prepared without tasting (cook must not put spoon in mouth). Cooked on low heat is critical. Made on Kharna day for offering.

name: Janmashtami Panjiri
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat flour (or coriander seed powder — dhania panjiri), 1 cup ghee, 1 cup powdered sugar, ¼ cup makhana (crushed), ¼ cup chopped almonds, ¼ cup chopped cashews, 2 tbsp raisins, 2 tbsp melon seeds (magaz), ½ tsp cardamom powder, ¼ tsp nutmeg powder
preparation: STEP 1: Heat ½ cup ghee in a heavy pan. Add flour. STEP 2: Roast on LOW heat, stirring continuously, for 15-20 minutes until golden brown and aromatic. This is the critical step. STEP 3: In a separate pan, dry roast makhana for 3 minutes. Crush coarsely. STEP 4: Add remaining ghee to the roasted flour. STEP 5: Turn off heat. Immediately add powdered sugar, crushed makhana, almonds, cashews, raisins, melon seeds. STEP 6: Add cardamom and nutmeg. Mix well. STEP 7: Cool completely. Offer to Krishna at midnight. STEP 8: Distribute as prasad.
tips: Traditionally offered to Krishna at midnight on Janmashtami. Also given to new mothers post-delivery for strength.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi Modak (Ukadiche)
ingredients: FOR OUTER: 1 cup rice flour, 1 cup water, 1 tsp ghee, ¼ tsp salt. FOR FILLING: 1 cup fresh coconut (grated), ¾ cup jaggery (grated), ¼ tsp cardamom powder, 1 tbsp poppy seeds (khus khus)
preparation: STEP 1 (FILLING): In a pan, combine grated coconut and jaggery. Cook on low heat, stirring often, for 8-10 minutes until jaggery melts and mixture thickens. STEP 2: Add cardamom and poppy seeds. Mix. Cool completely. STEP 3 (OUTER): Boil 1 cup water with ghee and salt. STEP 4: Reduce heat to low. Add rice flour all at once. Stir vigorously. STEP 5: Cover and let steam 2 minutes. Turn off heat. STEP 6: Transfer to a bowl. When warm enough to handle, knead with wet hands into a smooth soft dough. STEP 7 (ASSEMBLY): Grease palms with ghee. Take a small dough ball. Flatten with fingers into a small round cup. STEP 8: Fill with 1 tbsp coconut filling. Pinch edges into 5-6 pleats, bringing them together at the top like a bud. STEP 9: Repeat for 15-18 modaks. STEP 10 (STEAMING): Place modaks in a greased steamer. Steam for 10-12 minutes. STEP 11: Serve hot topped with ghee, offered first to Lord Ganesha.
tips: Lord Ganesha's favourite food. The pleating is a skill — practice makes perfect. Serve with warm ghee drizzled on top.

name: Eid Sheer Khurma
ingredients: Refer to Recipe R010
preparation: Refer to Recipe R010 in Ramadan Recipes sheet. Traditionally served for Eid ul-Fitr morning.
tips: The most iconic Eid dessert. Every Muslim household prepares this on Eid morning.

name: Onam Sadhya Sambar
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal, 1 cup mixed vegetables (drumstick, ladyfinger, brinjal, ash gourd, cucumber, pumpkin), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 lemon-sized ball of tamarind (soaked, extracted), 2 tsp sambar powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp jaggery, FOR TEMPERING: 2 tbsp coconut oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp fenugreek, 2 dry red chillies, 10 curry leaves, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Pressure cook toor dal with 3 cups water and turmeric for 4 whistles. Whisk smooth. STEP 2: In a pot, boil chopped vegetables (except tomato) with 2 cups water and salt for 10 minutes. STEP 3: Add tomatoes and tamarind extract. Boil 5 minutes. STEP 4: Add cooked dal and sambar powder. Simmer 10 minutes. STEP 5: Add jaggery. STEP 6: TEMPERING: Heat coconut oil. Add mustard seeds — let splutter. Add fenugreek, dry red chillies, curry leaves, asafoetida. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 7: Pour tempering over sambar. Garnish with coriander. Serve with steamed rice as part of Onam sadhya.
tips: Sambar is one of 26+ dishes on the Onam sadhya banana leaf. Kerala coconut oil is essential.

name: Diwali Gulab Jamun
ingredients: FOR JAMUNS: 1 cup milk powder (khoya alternative), ¼ cup maida (all-purpose flour), ¼ tsp baking soda, 3 tbsp milk (or as needed), 1 tsp ghee. FOR SYRUP: 1½ cups sugar, 1½ cups water, 4 cardamom pods (crushed), 1 tsp rose water, few saffron strands. FOR FRYING: ghee or oil
preparation: STEP 1 (SYRUP): Boil sugar and water. Add cardamom and saffron. Simmer 5 minutes until slightly sticky (not thread stage — thinner). Turn off heat. Add rose water. Keep warm. STEP 2 (DOUGH): Mix milk powder, maida, baking soda. Add ghee and rub in. Add milk 1 tbsp at a time. Knead into a soft, smooth dough. Do NOT over-knead. Rest 5 minutes. STEP 3: Divide into 15-18 small balls (grape-sized — they double in size). Roll smooth (no cracks). STEP 4 (FRYING): Heat ghee/oil on LOW-MEDIUM heat. Test: dough ball should sink and rise slowly. STEP 5: Fry 4-5 jamuns at a time. Roll gently to brown evenly. Fry 5-6 minutes until deep golden brown. STEP 6: Immediately transfer hot jamuns to warm sugar syrup. STEP 7: Soak 30 minutes minimum before serving. Serve warm or at room temperature.
tips: CRITICAL: LOW-MEDIUM heat frying. High heat = raw inside. Cracks in dough balls = jamuns will burst.

name: Shivratri Thandai
ingredients: FOR PASTE: 10 almonds, 15 cashews, 2 tbsp poppy seeds, 2 tbsp melon seeds, 2 tbsp fennel seeds, 1 tsp black peppercorns, 6 cardamom pods, 10 rose petals (dried). FOR MILK MIX: 1 litre cold milk, ¾ cup sugar, few saffron strands, ½ tsp cardamom powder, ice cubes
preparation: STEP 1: Soak almonds, cashews, poppy seeds, and melon seeds in warm water for 4 hours. STEP 2: Drain. Peel almonds. STEP 3: Grind everything (nuts + soaked seeds + fennel + peppercorns + cardamom + rose petals) with ½ cup milk into a smooth paste. STEP 4: Warm milk. Add sugar. Stir until dissolved. Cool. STEP 5: Add the nut paste. Mix well. STEP 6: Strain through a muslin cloth (squeeze out all liquid). STEP 7: Chill for 2 hours. STEP 8: Serve over ice, garnished with saffron and chopped nuts.
tips: The traditional Shivratri drink. Bhaang (cannabis) is added in some regions — this recipe is bhaang-free.

name: Ganesh Chaturthi Puran Poli
ingredients: Refer to Recipe J014 (Jain Puran Poli)
preparation: Refer to Recipe J014 in Jain Recipes sheet. Same recipe — traditional Ganesh Chaturthi and Diwali sweet.
tips: A staple in Maharashtrian celebrations. Naturally onion-garlic free.

name: Navratri Kanjak Prasad
ingredients: FOR KALA CHANA: 1 cup black chickpeas (soaked overnight), 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp amchur, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp ghee, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 2 tbsp coriander. FOR HALWA: 1 cup sooji, 1 cup ghee, 1 cup sugar, 3 cups water, ½ tsp cardamom, dry fruits. FOR PURI: 2 cups atta, ½ tsp salt, water
preparation: STEP 1 (CHANA): Pressure cook soaked chana with 3 cups water and salt for 5 whistles. STEP 2: Heat ghee. Add cumin, asafoetida. Add cooked chana with a little water. Add spices. Cook 5 minutes to thicken. STEP 3 (HALWA): Refer to Recipe W005 method (banana sheera) — same technique without banana. STEP 4 (PURI): Knead soft dough. Roll small puris. Deep fry. STEP 5: Serve all three together to 9 young girls (Kanjaks) on Ashtami/Navami with a coin/gift.
tips: Traditional prasad given to 9 young girls symbolizing the 9 forms of Durga on Navratri Ashtami. Non-fasting food — meant for after Navratri parana.

name: Sindhi Sai Bhaji (Guruvar Vrat)
ingredients: 2 cups mixed greens (palak, methi, dill), ½ cup chana dal (soaked), 1 medium eggplant (cubed), 1 potato (cubed) — skip if Jain, 1 tomato (chopped), 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, ½ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp salt, 2 green chillies, 2 cups water
preparation: STEP 1: Wash all greens thoroughly. Chop coarsely. STEP 2: In a pressure cooker, add chana dal, greens, eggplant, potato, tomato, green chillies, and 2 cups water. Add turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt. STEP 3: Pressure cook for 5 whistles. STEP 4: Open. Using a mathani (wooden churner) or immersion blender, mash coarsely — should not be totally smooth. STEP 5: In a small pan, heat ghee. Add cumin and asafoetida. Pour over sai bhaji. STEP 6: Simmer 5 minutes. Serve with plain rice or roti.
tips: Traditional Sindhi Thursday meal. Yellow chana dal fits the Thursday yellow theme. Highly nutritious.

name: Dal Tadka
ingredients: 1 cup toor dal (arhar), 4 cups water, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 large onion (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, FOR TADKA: 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dry red chillies, 8 curry leaves, ¼ tsp asafoetida, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: Wash toor dal. Pressure cook with 4 cups water, turmeric, salt, and chopped tomato + onion + ginger-garlic paste for 4 whistles. STEP 2: Open cooker. Whisk dal to a smooth consistency. If too thick, add ½ cup water. Simmer 3 minutes. STEP 3: TADKA: Heat ghee in a small pan. Add cumin and mustard seeds. Let them splutter. STEP 4: Add dry red chillies, curry leaves, asafoetida. Sauté 15 seconds. STEP 5: Add red chilli powder off the heat (to prevent burning). STEP 6: Pour tempering over dal. Garnish with coriander. Serve with rice or roti.
tips: The most staple Indian meal. Use fresh tomatoes for tanginess. Can substitute toor dal with moong or masoor.

name: Jeera Rice
ingredients: 1½ cups basmati rice (soaked 20 min), 3 cups water, 2 tbsp ghee, 2 tsp cumin seeds, 2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 4 green cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander leaves
preparation: STEP 1: Drain soaked rice. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pot. Add cumin seeds — let them splutter (30 seconds). STEP 3: Add bay leaves, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon. Sauté 20 seconds. STEP 4: Add drained rice. Sauté 1 minute (this coats the grains and prevents sticking). STEP 5: Add 3 cups water and salt. Bring to a boil. STEP 6: Cover with tight lid. Reduce heat to lowest. Cook 15 minutes. STEP 7: Turn off heat. Rest 5 minutes covered. STEP 8: Fluff with fork. Garnish with coriander.
tips: Perfect fluffy rice with distinct grains. Soaking is important for basmati.

name: Chapati/Roti
ingredients: 2 cups whole wheat flour (atta), 1 cup warm water, ½ tsp salt, 1 tsp oil, extra flour for dusting, ghee for spreading
preparation: STEP 1: In a bowl, mix flour and salt. Add oil. STEP 2: Add water gradually. Knead into a soft, smooth dough. Rest 15-20 minutes covered with a damp cloth. STEP 3: Divide into 8 equal balls. Roll each into a smooth round. STEP 4: Dust with flour. Roll into 6-inch circles, using minimal flour. STEP 5: Heat a tawa on medium-high heat. Place roti. STEP 6: Cook 20 seconds until small bubbles appear. Flip. STEP 7: Cook 30 seconds. Flip again. STEP 8: Using tongs, hold the roti directly over the flame (or on a gas ring) for 5-10 seconds — it should puff up. STEP 9: Apply ghee. Serve immediately.
tips: The direct-flame puffing is what makes a proper Indian roti. If using an electric stove, press the roti with a folded cloth on the tawa.

name: Aloo Gobi
ingredients: 1 medium cauliflower (florets), 3 potatoes (cubed), 1 large onion (chopped), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Heat oil in a kadai. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 2: Add chopped onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until golden. STEP 3: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 4: Add chopped tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until soft. STEP 5: Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder, and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 6: Add potato cubes. Sauté 2 minutes. STEP 7: Add cauliflower florets. Mix gently. STEP 8: Add ½ cup water. Cover and cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are tender. STEP 9: Sprinkle garam masala. Garnish with coriander. Serve with roti.
tips: The classic Punjabi combination. Do not overcook cauliflower — it should retain some texture.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
ingredients: 250g paneer (cubed), 3 large tomatoes (chopped), 1 large onion (chopped), 10 cashews, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 3 tbsp butter, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp red chilli powder (Kashmiri), 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, ½ cup cream, 1 tsp kasuri methi, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Soak cashews in warm water for 15 minutes. STEP 2: In a pan, boil chopped onion, tomatoes, and cashews with 1 cup water for 10 minutes. Cool. STEP 3: Blend to a smooth puree. Strain if you want restaurant-style silky texture. STEP 4: Heat butter in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add the puree. Cook 8-10 minutes until it thickens. STEP 7: Add red chilli powder, coriander powder, salt, and sugar. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 8: Add 1 cup water. Simmer 5 minutes. STEP 9: Add paneer cubes. Simmer 3 minutes. STEP 10: Add cream and garam masala. STEP 11: Crush kasuri methi between palms and add. STEP 12: Garnish with coriander. Serve with naan or rice.
tips: The Indian restaurant classic. Straining the puree is what gives that silky texture. Kasuri methi at the end adds distinctive aroma.

name: Rajma Chawal
ingredients: 1 cup rajma (kidney beans — soaked overnight), 2 large onions (chopped), 3 tomatoes (pureed), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp garam masala, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 4 cups water, 2 tbsp coriander, 1½ cups basmati rice (cooked separately as jeera rice)
preparation: STEP 1: Pressure cook soaked rajma with 4 cups water, salt, and turmeric for 6-7 whistles until soft. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 3: Add chopped onion. Sauté 5 minutes until deep golden. STEP 4: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add tomato puree. Cook 8-10 minutes until oil separates. STEP 6: Add red chilli powder, coriander powder. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 7: Add cooked rajma with its water. Mash a few rajma with the back of the spoon for thicker gravy. STEP 8: Simmer 15 minutes on low heat, stirring occasionally. STEP 9: Add garam masala. Adjust salt. Garnish with coriander. STEP 10: Serve hot with jeera rice.
tips: The comfort food of North India. Slow-cooking rajma is what develops flavour. Do not skip soaking overnight.

name: Chole (Chana Masala)
ingredients: 1 cup kabuli chana (chickpeas — soaked overnight), 2 large onions (chopped), 3 tomatoes (pureed), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 green chillies, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 2 tsp chole masala, 1 tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp amchur (dry mango powder), 2 tea bags (for dark colour) or 1 tsp tea leaves in muslin cloth, 4 cups water, 2 tbsp coriander
preparation: STEP 1: Pressure cook chana with 4 cups water, salt, and 2 tea bags (for the traditional dark colour) for 6-7 whistles. Remove tea bags. STEP 2: Heat ghee in a pan. Add cumin. STEP 3: Add onion. Sauté 5 minutes until deep golden. STEP 4: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 5: Add tomato puree. Cook 8-10 minutes until oil separates. STEP 6: Add chole masala, red chilli powder, turmeric. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 7: Add cooked chana with water. Simmer 15 minutes. STEP 8: Add amchur. Cook 2 more minutes. STEP 9: Garnish with coriander. Serve with bhature, kulcha, or rice.
tips: The tea trick is the secret to the deep colour of Punjabi chole. Amchur adds the traditional tangy finish.

name: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 2 bunches spinach (blanched), 250g paneer (cubed), 1 onion (chopped), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 green chillies, 2 tbsp ghee, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp red chilli powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1 tsp salt, ¼ cup cream
preparation: STEP 1: Blanch spinach for 2 minutes. Plunge in ice water. Squeeze dry. Blend with green chillies to a smooth puree. STEP 2: Lightly sauté paneer in 1 tsp ghee. Set aside. STEP 3: Heat ghee. Add cumin — let splutter. STEP 4: Add onion. Sauté 4 minutes. STEP 5: Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 30 seconds. STEP 6: Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes. STEP 7: Add red chilli powder and salt. Sauté 1 minute. STEP 8: Add spinach puree. Mix. Cook 5 minutes on low heat. STEP 9: Add paneer and ½ cup water. Simmer 3 minutes. STEP 10: Add cream and garam masala. Serve with roti or naan.
tips: Blanching + ice water shock preserves the bright green colour. Do not overcook after adding spinach — it turns dark.

name: Vegetable Biryani
ingredients: 2 cups basmati rice (soaked 30 min), 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, cauliflower, peas), 2 onions (sliced, fried), 1 cup curd (whisked), 2 tomatoes (chopped), 2 tbsp biryani masala, 2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 2 green chillies, 1 tsp red chilli powder, ½ tsp turmeric, 2 tsp salt, ½ cup ghee, ¼ cup mint (chopped), ¼ cup coriander, saffron in ¼ cup milk, whole spices (2 bay leaves, 4 cloves, 4 cardamom, 1 inch cinnamon)
preparation: STEP 1: Marinate vegetables with curd, ginger-garlic paste, ½ biryani masala, red chilli powder, turmeric, and salt. Rest 30 minutes. STEP 2: Boil 4 cups water with whole spices and salt. Add drained rice. Cook 70% done. Drain. STEP 3: Heat ¼ cup ghee in a heavy pot. Add ½ fried onions and green chillies. STEP 4: Add marinated vegetables. Cook covered 10 minutes. STEP 5: Add tomatoes and remaining biryani masala. Cook 5 minutes. STEP 6: Layer half the rice on top. Sprinkle mint, coriander, fried onions, and 2 tbsp ghee. STEP 7: Add remaining rice. Top with remaining mint, coriander, fried onions, saffron milk, and ghee. STEP 8: Cover tightly. Cook on very low heat 20 minutes (dum). STEP 9: Rest 10 minutes. Fluff gently. Serve with raita.
tips: Vegetarian version of the classic. Dum cooking is essential for the layered flavour.
